prompt: How do I set a single page to landscape in the middle of a document in Word?
completion:
Below is a quick, step‑by‑step guide that works in virtually every recent version of Microsoft Word (2010–2021, Office 365, Word for Mac, etc.). The idea is simple: **break the document into sections, change the orientation of the section that contains the page you want, then return to the original orientation.** --- ## 1. Insert a Section Break before the page you want to go Landscape | Windows | Mac | |---------|-----| | **Word 2010–2021 / Office 365**
1. Put your cursor at the very start of the page you want Landscape.
2. Go to **Layout** > **Breaks**.
3. Choose **Section Breaks** > **Next Page**. | **Word 2016–2021 / Office 365 for Mac**
1. Put your cursor at the very start of the page you want Landscape.
2. Go to **Layout** > **Breaks**.
3. Choose **Section Breaks** > **Next Page**. | | **Word 2007**
Same as above – the **Page Layout** tab replaces **Layout**. | **Word 2011 and earlier**
Same as above – the **Layout** tab replaces **Page Layout**. | > **Tip:** To make the break visible, click **¶** (Show/Hide) on the Home tab. Section breaks appear as a dotted line with the word “Section Break (Next Page)”. --- ## 2. Change that section’s orientation to Landscape | Windows | Mac | |---------|-----| | **Word 2010–2021 / Office 365**
1. Click anywhere on the page that you just made part of the new section.
2. Go to **Layout** > **Orientation** > **Landscape**. | **Word 2016–2021 / Office 365 for Mac**
1. Click anywhere on the page that you just made part of the new section.
2. Go to **Layout** > **Orientation** > **Landscape**. | | **Word 2007**
Same steps – use **Page Layout** > **Orientation**. | **Word 2011 and earlier**
Same steps – use **Layout** > **Orientation**. | > After you click **Landscape**, the entire section (i.e., the single page you wanted) will flip to landscape while the rest of the document stays portrait. --- ## 3. Return to Portrait for the following page(s) 1. Move your cursor to the *first page after* the landscape page. 2. Insert another **Section Break (Next Page)** (same as step 1). 3. Click anywhere on the page that follows the landscape page, then go to **Layout** > **Orientation** > **Portrait**. > **Result:** > *Section 1* – portrait (all pages before the break) > *Section 2* – landscape (the single page) > *Section 3* – portrait (all pages after the break) --- ## 4. (Optional) Adjust margins for the landscape page If the landscape page looks cramped or you want a custom margin: 1. With the cursor still on the landscape page, open **Layout** > **Margins** > **Custom Margins** (or **Page Setup** on older versions). 2. In the **Margins** tab, set the values you prefer. 3. **Important:** Make sure the **Apply to** dropdown is set to **This section**. --- ## 5. Quick Summary (one‑liner) > 1. **Section Break (Next Page)** at the start of the page. > 2. **Orientation → Landscape** for that section. > 3. **Section Break (Next Page)** after that page. > 4. **Orientation → Portrait** for the following section. --- ## 6. Troubleshooting & Extra Tips | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **Page number runs into the wrong section** | Ensure the “Header & Footer” are set to “Link to Previous” appropriately. You might need to unlink the footer in the new section. | | **Section breaks are missing** | Turn on “Show/Hide” (¶) to make them visible. | | **Orientation doesn’t change** | Double‑check that you’re in the correct section. Section breaks are required; Word can’t change the orientation of a single page within the same section. | | **You need more than one landscape page** | Insert a **Section Break (Next Page)** before the first landscape page and one after the last landscape page. Then set the middle section to Landscape. | | **Using Word Online** | As of 2026, Word Online does not support section breaks. Use the desktop version or a workaround (e.g., insert a table and rotate the table). | --- ### Quick “One‑Click” Cheat‑Sheet (Windows 365): 1. **Layout** → **Breaks** → **Next Page** 2. **Layout** → **Orientation** → **Landscape** 3. **Layout** → **Breaks** → **Next Page** 4. **Layout** → **Orientation** → **Portrait** --- That’s it! By sandwiching the page you want in its own section and flipping that section’s orientation, you can have a single landscape page (or any number of consecutive pages) in an otherwise portrait document. Happy formatting!
